length: Term 2 Weeks 1–7 · 18 lessons including 9 labs, plus the test and the EPI
description: Building on the particle model, students classify matter as pure substances or mixtures, including solutions, and use particle diagrams to tell them apart. They explain dissolving, saturation and solubility with particles and read solubility curves, then choose and justify separation techniques — decanting, filtration, magnetic separation, evaporation, crystallisation, distillation and chromatography — from the property that differs between the parts of a mixture. A hands-on lab each week builds to the CAT (EPI): recovering salt from rock salt.
notes: **Lesson rows follow the 2027 scope and sequence** (T2 W1–W7), reordered 23 Nov 2026 so every lab follows its theory lesson and Filtration comes before the EPI. Lessons are numbered by their place in the unit; the CATs are not numbered.
Theory comes from the Separation Lesson Booklets (A5, Book 1 = Lessons 1–7, Book 2 = Lessons 8–16); the labs from the Separation Experiment Booklet (A4, Experiments 1–9).
**CAT (EPI) = recovering salt from rock salt.** The solubility and temperature investigation runs as Lesson 13. {{PH:rock salt investigation booklet — still to be written}}
**No site unit or slide decks exist for this unit yet**, so explicit instruction links are placeholders.

achievement.text: Classify matter as pure substances or mixtures, including solutions, using particle diagrams; explain dissolving and solubility with particles; select and justify techniques to separate mixtures based on the different properties of their components.

Plan fair, safe investigations; select equipment to measure mass, volume, temperature and time precisely; organise data in tables and graphs; analyse patterns and anomalies; evaluate methods and sources of error; communicate findings.
Examine how different perspectives contribute to science — First Nations food processing and water purification techniques (Lesson 10).

descriptors.text: Matter can be classified as pure substances such as elements and compounds or impure substances such as mixtures (including solutions); mixtures can be separated using the different properties of their components — filtration, decanting, evaporation, crystallisation, magnetic separation, distillation and chromatography
The particle model explains dissolving and the properties of substances
Multidisciplinary endeavours draw on different perspectives and worldviews — First Nations separation techniques
Science inquiry — questioning and predicting (I01); planning and conducting (I02–I03); processing, modelling and analysing (I04–I05); evaluating (I06–I07); communicating (I08)
Levels 7–8, above level in this unit — elements, compounds, symbols and formulas (Part D only)

prepare: Opening review of the particle model and particle diagrams from Term 1.
Stile *1.1 What are mixtures?* as a pre-unit check.
review: Booklet Part C checked in class; a lab write-up each week.
Mixtures revision: Mixtures Quiz, Practice MCQ and Practice Written Response (Mixtures), Mixtures flashcards (faculty folder); Stile *Mixtures Lab — Revision*.
diff: A classification flowchart; a technique-chooser table (property that differs → technique); pre-drawn graph axes.
Worked first row in red on every results table; sentence starters for conclusions.
extension: Part D of each booklet lesson — elements and compounds (VC2S8U07), designing a multi-step separation.

lessons.title: Pure substances
li: Explain what “pure” means in science.
Represent pure substances with particle diagrams.
Use melting and boiling points to test purity.
sc: I can tell a pure substance from a mixture and give evidence.

lessons.title: Mixtures
li: Classify matter as pure substances, such as elements and compounds, or impure substances such as mixtures, including solutions (VC2S8U06).
Identify uniform and non-uniform mixtures.
Explain why mixtures can be separated.
sc: I can classify an everyday material as a pure substance or a mixture, and say whether a mixture is uniform.
guided: **Stile:** 1.1 What are mixtures? · 1.2 The properties of mixtures · 2.1 Suspensions and colloids
review: Card sort checked as a class

lessons.title: Lab: solubility
li: Test which substances dissolve in water.
sc: I can sort substances into soluble and insoluble using my observations.
explicit: Lab briefing — safety and the fair-test rules

prac.name: Solubility — testing a set of household solids in water
prac.si: Plan a fair test by keeping the amount of solid and water the same; record observations in a table (VC2S8I02, VC2S8I03).
prac.su: Classify substances as soluble or insoluble (VC2S8U06).

lessons.title: Classifying from particle diagrams
li: Use a flowchart to classify particle diagrams as pure or mixture, and by state.
Draw my own particle diagrams of pure substances and mixtures.
sc: I can classify a substance from a particle diagram and explain my choice.

lessons.title: Solute, solvent and solution
li: Explain dissolving with particles; use solute, solvent, solution, soluble and insoluble correctly.
Explain that mass is conserved when a solid dissolves.
Describe solutions as concentrated or dilute.
sc: I can label the solute, solvent and solution in an example and draw the particles.

lessons.title: Lab: surface area and solubility
li: Investigate how particle size changes how fast a solid dissolves.
sc: I can name my variables and explain my result using particles.

prac.name: Surface area and dissolving — sugar cube vs granulated vs caster sugar
prac.si: Write a hypothesis; identify independent, dependent and controlled variables; time each trial and repeat (VC2S8I01, VC2S8I02).
prac.su: Explain with particles why a larger surface area dissolves faster (VC2S8U05).

lessons.title: Decanting, filtration and magnetic separation
li: Choose a separation technique from the property that differs.
Explain sieving, winnowing, decanting, filtration and magnetic separation, including First Nations food processing (VC2S8H02).
sc: I can choose and justify a technique to separate a mixture.
explicit: {{PH:PPT link — Decanting, Filtration and Magnetic Separation}}
review: Technique choices checked — the test and EPI depend on them

lessons.title: Evaporation and crystallisation
li: Get a dissolved solid back by evaporating to dryness or by crystallisation.
Use dissolving as a step in a separation.
sc: I can describe how to get salt back from salty water, and explain each step.

lessons.title: Lab: fast and slow evaporation
li: Observe how the rate of evaporation changes the crystals left behind.
sc: I can compare crystals from fast and slow evaporation and explain the difference.

prac.name: Fast and slow evaporation — salt solution evaporated over a Bunsen burner and on a windowsill
prac.si: Make and record careful observations, including sketches, over time (VC2S8I03).
prac.su: Explain evaporation of the solvent with particles (VC2S8U05).

lessons.title: Soluble and saturation
li: Explain what a saturated solution is.
Give solubility as a number and scale it to other volumes.
Describe how temperature changes solubility.
sc: I can tell whether a solution is saturated from the amount dissolved.

lessons.title: CAT — Test
li: Show what I know about pure substances, mixtures, solutions, saturation and separation techniques.
sc: I can classify, explain dissolving and saturation, and choose a separation technique under test conditions.
guided: Revision: Mixtures Quiz, Practice MCQ (Mixtures), Practice Written Response (Mixtures) {{PH:test paper}}

lessons.title: Lab: rates of evaporation
li: Investigate a factor that changes how fast water evaporates.
sc: I can name my variables, measure mass loss over time and graph it.
explicit: Lab briefing — choosing a variable (surface area, temperature or air flow)

prac.name: Rates of evaporation — mass of water lost over time
prac.si: Write an aim, a hypothesis and a repeatable method; weigh to 0.1 g at intervals and graph the mass lost (VC2S8I01, VC2S8I02, VC2S8I04).
prac.su: Explain the effect of the variable on evaporation using particles (VC2S8U05).

lessons.title: Solubility gradients (solubility curves)
li: Read and draw a solubility curve.
Use a curve to predict how much will dissolve, and the crystals formed on cooling.
sc: I can read a solubility curve and use it to predict how much will dissolve.

lessons.title: Lab: solubility and temperature
li: Measure how much potassium nitrate dissolves at one temperature, and pool the class data into a solubility curve.
sc: I can plot class data as a solubility curve, draw a line of best fit and describe the trend.
explicit: Lab briefing — reaching saturation; potassium nitrate is an oxidiser

prac.name: Solubility and temperature — potassium nitrate in 10 mL of water at 20–60 °C (class data pooled)
prac.si: Measure mass and temperature precisely; plot the class data as a solubility curve and describe the trend (VC2S8I03, VC2S8I04, VC2S8I05).
prac.su: Explain with particles why more solute dissolves at higher temperatures (VC2S8U06).

review: Class curve compared with published values

lessons.title: Lab: growing copper sulfate crystals
li: Grow crystals from a saturated solution.
sc: I can explain why crystals form as a saturated solution cools or evaporates.
explicit: Lab briefing — handling copper sulfate safely

prac.name: Growing CuSO₄ crystals — saturated solution, seed crystal, left to grow (stretch)
prac.si: Follow a method safely and record observations over several days (VC2S8I03).
prac.su: Link crystallisation to saturation and solubility (VC2S8U06).

lessons.title: Lab: filtration
li: Separate an insoluble solid from a liquid by filtration, and compare three filters fairly.
sc: I can set up a filter funnel and name the residue and the filtrate.

prac.name: Filtration — filter paper, a coffee filter and cotton cloth compared on muddy water
prac.si: Set up filtration correctly; compare three filters in a fair test, timing each and rating the filtrate (VC2S8I02, VC2S8I03).

review: Residue and filtrate labelled; filters compared — needed for the EPI next week

lessons.title: Distillation and chromatography
li: Explain how distillation gets the solvent back.
Separate dyes with chromatography.
Describe how drinking water is made.
sc: I can label a distillation set-up and explain what happens at each part.
guided: Paper chromatography of marker inks (in class)

lessons.title: Lab: distillation
li: Collect pure water from salty or inky water by distillation.
sc: I can explain why the distillate is pure, and test it.
explicit: Demonstration or lab briefing — distillation set-up and hazards

prac.name: Distillation — collecting pure water from coloured salt water
prac.si: Use equipment safely and record observations of each stage (VC2S8I03).
prac.su: Explain distillation with evaporation and condensation (VC2S8U06).

lessons.title: CAT (EPI) — recovering salt from rock salt
li: Plan and carry out a separation: dissolve, filter and evaporate.
Calculate percentage yield, explain losses and evaluate the method.
Communicate findings using scientific vocabulary (VC2S8I08).
sc: I can calculate percentage yield and explain why it is less than 100%.

prac.name: Recovering salt from rock salt — dissolve, filter, evaporate; weigh and calculate yield
prac.si: Plan a method, record masses precisely and evaluate sources of error (VC2S8I02, VC2S8I03, VC2S8I06).
prac.su: Justify each separation step from the properties of salt, sand and water (VC2S8U06).

guided: The salt needs to dry overnight before weighing — weigh in the next lesson

lessons.title: Lab: Great Green Mix Up (GGMU)
li: Choose and carry out separation techniques to separate a mixture, using the properties of its parts.
sc: I can justify each separation step from a property that differs.
explicit: Lab briefing — check the booklet version against the faculty Great Green Mix Up sheet

prac.name: Great Green Mix Up — existing faculty experiment
prac.si: Use equipment safely and record observations of each step (VC2S8I03).
prac.su: Justify each separation technique from the properties of the mixture’s parts (VC2S8U06).
